requirements.requirement: The account datauser exists and is configured to use and own /srv/data.
requirements.summary: datauser was absent initially, then created as UID/GID 1001 with /srv/data as its home; the directory is owned by datauser and mode 0750. This state remained after restart.

requirements.requirement: Filesystem-level enforcement limits datauser to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data.
requirements.summary: The ext3 filesystem reports matching 102,400 KiB soft and hard user-quota limits. Direct writes by datauser inside /srv/data stopped with “Disk quota exceeded” at the limit, both before and after restart. /srv/data resides on the quota-enabled root filesystem, so the filesystem enforces the limit; this also means the UID quota applies across that filesystem, not exclusively to the directory.

requirements.requirement: The quota remains effective while retaining the installed operating-system release and kernel and using legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged. The native Gutsy quota 3.14-8 package was installed, usrquota persisted in fstab, and a completed restart showed a new boot identity, the remounted quota-enabled ext3 filesystem, unchanged limits, preserved data, renewed enforcement, and recovered SSH.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct enforcement and restart-persistence evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart quota/data state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered quota, data, filesystem, and SSH state.
limitations: The lifecycle collector could not inspect failed services because systemctl is unsupported on this legacy release.

The lifecycle listening-socket snapshots were empty even though the executor directly observed sshd listening after restart; successful post-restart SSH commands and process/listener evidence substantially mitigate this collector inconsistency.
No final command explicitly inspected or removed the fstab backup, so its retained status is inferred from its successful creation and the complete timeline containing no cleanup.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations were causally related to installing, configuring, testing, or restart-verifying the quota. Oversized test files were removed. Two low-risk evidence/rollback artifacts were unnecessarily retained: /etc/fstab.pre-datauser-quota, created as a backup with no later cleanup, and /srv/data/restart-marker, created for persistence verification and still present in the final directory listing. The failed legacy-incompatible useradd attempt showed no mutation. Package health remained clean and the bounded /tmp inventory was empty after execution.
